title: Cardinality-aware token telemetry and adaptive quantile sketching for alert noise reduction
author: Miguel Ortega
description:
Motivation: We see a class of noisy SLI alerts driven by high-cardinality token-paths (rare prefixes or model->tool call combos). Root cause is twofold: (1) existing token cost histograms and span sampling miss long-tail cardinality signals, and (2) alert thresholds are static percentiles that overfit recent bursty traffic. This PR introduces a small telemetry pipeline plus on-host adaptive quantile sketches to surface cardinality-aware token metrics and a companion Grafana dashboard and alert tuning recipe.

Design summary: implement a compact P2-like quantile sketch for token-cost and token-latency streams, keyed by a reduced token-path fingerprint (service:model:route:tool), with reservoir-backed microtraces for top-k fingerprints. We also add a periodic join job that materializes top-N cardinality contributors and emits both sketch summaries and a low-volume aggregated sample per contributor for linkage to traces. The pipeline is designed to be conservative on ingestion volume (sketch + counts) and to integrate with existing span_enricher hooks.

Checklist:
- [x] core sketch implementation (telemetry/ingest/quantile_sketch.go)
- [x] fingerprinting and cardinality reducer (telemetry/pipeline/token_fingerprint.go)
- [x] span enrichment for linking sketches to traces (pkg/trace/span_enricher/annotator.go)
- [x] dashboard & alerts (dashboards/observability/token-cardinality-dashboard.json)
- [x] synthetic load test and regression e2e (tests/e2e/token-telemetry.test.ts, scripts/synthetic-load/token-cardinality-checker.yaml)
- [x] docs and rollout notes (docs/telemetry/token-cardinality.md)

Commits summary: [1/6] Add quantile sketch data structure and unit tests; [2/6] Fingerprint reducer and sketching pipeline integration; [3/6] Bridge to span enricher and minimal microtrace reservoir; [4/6] Dashboard and alert rules; [5/6] End-to-end synthetic load test and CI; [6/6] Docs, changelog and rollout policy.

Files changed (high level): services/telemetry/collector/token_telemetry.go (ingest adapter), services/telemetry/ingest/quantile_sketch.go (core algorithm, ~380 loc), services/telemetry/pipeline/token_fingerprint.go (cardinality reducer), pkg/trace/span_enricher/annotator.go (adds sketch_id annotation), dashboards/observability/token-cardinality-dashboard.json (new dashboard), scripts/synthetic-load/token-cardinality-checker.yaml (k6 scenario), tests/e2e/token-telemetry.test.ts (CI e2e), docs/telemetry/token-cardinality.md (design + rollout), CI config tweak (.github/workflows/telemetry-e2e.yml).

Small illustrative snippet (sketch API):
- UpdateSketch(key, value)  -- idempotent, lock-free for typical path sizes
- MergeSketch(other)        -- used by the joiner job

Testing & validation: Ran e2e with synthetic traffic that injects 50k unique token-path fingerprints over 10m and verified (a) sketch estimates track median/p95 within tolerance; (b) synthetic-alert-runbook reduces alert flapping by ~62% in the noisy scenario; (c) end-to-end trace linkage works for top-100 contributors. CI: all unit tests + telemetry-e2e passed in the PR run.

Rollout plan: staged rollout: start with telemetry-sandbox region -> canary on 10% of traffic using a new telemetry feature flag -> full roll once we observe stable resource usage and alert noise reduction for 72h. The dashboard contains a "feature:token-cardinality" panel that operators can use to validate.

Backward compatibility: sketches are additive and do not change existing metrics, we expose new metric names with a v1 suffix. No breaking changes expected.

Related work: this complements previous per-route watermarks and token attribution PRs by focusing on cardinality and sketch-based percentiles rather than raw histograms. Linear: ENG-2142, ENG-2217.

Notes: the quantile sketch implementation is intentionally conservative (memory-limited by default) and configurable via telemetry agent flags. Operator docs include suggested thresholds and an alert tuning recipe that migrates static percentile alerts to a hybrid rule (sketch-derived percentile + contributor-count gating).

feat(trace): annotate spans with sketch_id for linkage
chore(dashboards): token-cardinality dashboard and alert rules
test(e2e): synthetic cardinality load and regression checks
review_comments: Aisha Kaur: Nice approach — can we make the sketch window size dynamically configurable via the feature flag? I worry about memory on small agents.
Miguel Ortega: Added a flag (telemetry.sketch_window) with sane defaults and documented in pkg/config/telemetry_flags.go; the default keeps memory < 8MB/agent.
Claire Zhang: Can the top-N joiner be back-pressured? High-cardinality bursts could cause CPU spikes on the joiner job.
Miguel Ortega: Joiner uses a token-bucket admission and will shed to sketch-only mode under sustained overload; added metrics to surface shed events.
Evan Malik: Dashboard looks good — consider adding a compact flamegraph panel to show contributor overlap across models.
Miguel Ortega: Added a flamegraph panel and a note in the docs about interpreting contributor overlap.
Aisha Kaur: Approved after minor doc tweaks.
release_notes: Add cardinality-aware token telemetry: quantile sketches, top-N contributor joiner, span linkage, dashboard, and alert tuning guidance. Reduces alert flapping for long-tail token paths.
